hypothesis: A first 1H close at least 0.5–1.5 ATR away from the completed-session VWAP mean-reverts over the next 1–4 hourly bars enough to overcome modeled transaction costs.
parameter_rationale: Three ATR distance thresholds and three short holding horizons form a preregistered 3×3 grid. Session VWAP and ATR14 are fixed to isolate the deviation and holding-horizon effects.
baseline: 25% long buy-and-hold on same 1H candles, next-open execution, same cost model.
signal_rule: Session VWAP is cumulative sum(typical_price × volume)/sum(volume) over completed 1H bars with the same Moscow market date, using typical_price=(high+low+close)/3. ATR14 is a causal SMA of true range. After at least three bars of the session, enter long on first completed close below VWAP−k×ATR, short on first completed close above VWAP+k×ATR. No repeated signal while outside band. At signal close schedule an opposite exit after h further completed 1H bars. Entries and exits execute at following bar open; no same-bar fill. A new entry is suppressed until the scheduled exit signal. Position may cross a session or weekend and is marked to market each complete month.
cost_status: after_30bps_round_trip_transaction_cost_equivalent; excludes dividends, short borrow and exchange lots
selection: Compare median complete-calendar-month and calendar-year outcomes across all eligible stocks to buy-and-hold; inspect trade frequency and cost sensitivity. Research only; no paper promotion without signal parity and corporate-action review.
limitations: This is a 1H short-horizon strategy, not guaranteed flat at the end of each session; exits can execute next day.
Hourly OHLC bars cannot reconstruct intrabar execution or order-book spread.
Model uses 15 bps per side but does not separately model actual spread, borrow, dividends, lots or tax.
